A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MR-LFADS research. All 24 pages of each version, including Appendices A–F, equations, tables and figures, support comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original experiments on 37 synthetic datasets and original analyses of mouse electrophysiology, including photoinhibition prediction and inference consistency across seeds.

after.justification: v4 retains these original synthetic experiments and electrophysiology analyses in Sections 4–5 and the appendices.

M1.justification: MR-LFADS retains the same architecture, causal input inference, rate-derived communication, structured KL regularization and model variants. The revised RRR equations concern a comparator, not the proposed model.

E1.justification: Both versions use the memory and pass-decision networks, 35 randomly configured three- or four-region networks, and the same mouse electrophysiology sessions and test scenarios.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged, but Appendix A.2 revises RRR's stated per-region projection: Eq. 18 decomposes X times the ridge-weight block instead of the block alone. This changes the reported comparator specification; the PDFs do not establish an implementation change or rerun.

E3.justification: The synthetic 85%/15% trial split, 10% neuron holdout, evaluation metrics, training budgets and hyperparameters remain unchanged. No new evaluation protocol accompanies the RRR equation revisions.

E4.justification: The input-inference and communication-source ablations, consistency analyses, KL-channel analysis and factor-space SVD analysis are retained. Appendix C.2 rephrases the existing non-Gaussian stimulus rationale without adding a robustness experiment.

E5.justification: Both versions report ten seeds for Experiments 1–2, one fit per synthetic dataset in Experiment 3, and five seeds for electrophysiology consistency. Box-plot conventions, standard deviations, bootstrapping and significance-testing practices are unchanged.

E6.justification: Reported numerical outcomes, plotted results, rankings and qualitative findings match throughout Figures 2–5 and S1–S5. The p-values and supplementary numerical entries are also retained; the RRR equation edits have no accompanying result updates.

T1.justification: Appendix A.2 adds the previously missing rank constraint to Eq. 16's intermediate minimization and removes an optimizer-independent residual term. Eq. 18 changes the SVD argument from the ridge-weight block to X times that block. Other mathematical content is retained.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and discussion retain the same contributions and claims about disentangling communication, outperforming existing methods, predicting held-out perturbation effects and improving consistency across initializations.

C2.justification: The mechanism interpretations and limitations remain unchanged, including hyperparameter sensitivity and confounding from unobserved common inputs. Appendix C.2's revised robustness wording restates its existing rationale.

D1.justification: The revised RRR projection equations change the technical instructions available for reproducing that comparator, although the source-specific interpretation of X in Eq. 18 remains unclear. Hyperparameter tables, tuning schedules, software references, data preparation and access information are unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited works and research positioning are retained. Two Semedo references change the author entry from 'Byron, M. Y.' to 'Yu, B. M.'; these are bibliographic corrections to the same works.

P1.justification: Localized editing corrects grammar in Appendix C, clarifies that Gaussian posteriors are approximate, and corrects reference author names. The narrative and section organization remain substantially unchanged.

P2.justification: Equation 16 is reformatted into a more compact display with explicit constraints, alongside small spacing and page-flow adjustments. All five main figures, five supplementary figures and four supplementary tables retain their content and structure.

improvement.justification: v4 improves wording and restores a missing rank constraint in Eq. 16. However, Eq. 18 newly multiplies a per-region weight block by X while X remains defined as all source regions concatenated, leaving dimensional and implementation ambiguity. These mathematical benefits and drawbacks, with unchanged empirical evidence, prevent a reliable net-quality judgment.
